processing: Ripe pu-erh using slightly larger, lower-grade leaf, pressed into cakes. Informal readings of the number would make grade 9 the main leaf.
harvest_season: Not tied to one picking: it is a blend of fermented material.
appearance_dry: A 357 g dark brown cake of larger, lower-grade leaf.
appearance_liquor: Deep mahogany brown and clear, with a reddish rim.
appearance_wet: Large soft dark leaves, as usual for a lower-grade ripe blend.
taste_profile: One seller describes a smooth, medium-bodied cup of aged wood, autumn leaves and light caramel sweetness, with no bitterness.

brewing.notes: Larger leaf takes time to give flavour, so steep a little longer than for a fine ripe tea. Boiling water suits it.

vintage_note: Sold by year and batch, as 357 g cakes, with a 2023 pressing among those on sale. It is a budget recipe rather than a collector piece, so buy it for daily drinking.
description:
7592 is the plain sibling of the famous 7572, a Menghai Tea Factory ripe cake that is meant to be drunk rather than collected. By one seller's account it was designed in 1975 as a cheaper alternative, with slightly larger leaf at a lower grade.

Informal readings of Menghai numbers would make the third digit, 9, the main leaf grade, which fits that description, though it is not a factory statement.

The same seller describes a clear, deep mahogany cup with aged wood, autumn leaves and light caramel, and no bitterness. It takes boiling water and slightly longer steeps well.

Buy by batch and compare it with 7572 if you want to learn what grade does to a ripe tea.
history: A seller dates the recipe to 1975 at the Menghai factory, as an economical counterpart to 7572; no factory record of that date is at hand. Batches are still being made, as a 2023 pressing shows.
